blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Recovering metric world-space hand motion from egocentric video supports understanding human interactions and transferring them to embodied agents. Three challenges complicate this task: multi-stage pipelines propagate errors from independently estimated hand and camera motion; monocular observations leave physical scale ambiguous; and occlusion and out-of-view hands admit multiple plausible motion trajectories. We present DewHand, a unified model for direct joint reconstruction of world-space hand and camera motion. To avoid compounding errors from multi-stage estimation, DewHand jointly predicts hand and camera motion in a shared world coordinate system within a single-stage pipeline. To resolve metric-scale ambiguity, it combines scene-level geometric features from VGGT-$Ω$ with metric-space supervision, while hand-specific features preserve fine-grained articulation. To handle occlusion and out-of-view hands, we formulate reconstruction as conditional motion generation with flow matching. Under the same architecture, this generative formulation outperforms direct regression in both accuracy and temporal smoothness with only two sampling steps. Experiments on HOT3D and ARCTIC demonstrate improved world-space accuracy and temporal consistency over state-of-the-art methods. DewHand reduces rigid-aligned world-space error relative to StableHand from 32.9 to 28.4 mm on HOT3D and from 76.2 to 36.2 mm on ARCTIC. It also recovers camera scale within 10% on two thirds of HOT3D clips, versus about a quarter for SLAM. Moreover, in zero-shot evaluations on HoloAssist, H2O, and TACO, captured with different devices, DewHand achieves the lowest rigid-aligned world-space error (WA-MPJPE) on each dataset.

blocks.en:
Hands are our primary means of interacting with the physical world. Recovering their 3D motion
from wearable cameras can support the analysis of human activity, the capture of manipulation
skills, and the transfer of human demonstrations to embodied agents. These applications require
more than an accurate hand pose in each video frame: they require a metrically scaled trajectory in
a stable world coordinate system, so that a hand remains correctly placed as both the wearer and the
camera move.

blocks.en:
This work addresses world-space 3D hand motion reconstruction from monocular egocentric video.
Given a video, the goal is to recover the time-varying pose of both hands in a common world frame.
Consider a wearer reaching for an object while turning their head. In camera coordinates, even a
stationary hand appears to move with the camera; conversely, camera motion can hide or amplify the
hand’s motion in the image. A useful reconstruction must separate these effects and preserve the
hand’s position relative to the surrounding scene throughout the interaction.

blocks.en:
Three challenges motivate our formulation. First, accurate local hand reconstruction does not by
itself ensure a consistent world-space trajectory. Despite strong per-frame estimators ( Pavlakos et al., 2024 ; Potamias et al., 2025 ) ,
existing world-space pipelines typically estimate hands and camera motion separately, compose their
outputs, and optionally apply temporal optimization or motion-prior refinement ( Zhang et al., 2025a ; Yu et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Zeng et al., 2026 ) .
Camera drift and mismatches between these estimates can therefore propagate into the reconstructed
hand motion. Second, monocular video provides projective observations rather than direct metric
measurements, leaving physical scale ambiguous even when local articulation is accurately recovered.
Third, self-occlusion, hand-object interactions, motion blur, and frequent exits from the field of
view make hand observations incomplete. The visible evidence may be consistent with multiple motion
trajectories, motivating a conditional distribution over hand and camera motion.

blocks.en:
We introduce DewHand , a unified model that directly generates metric world-space
motion of both hands and the camera from egocentric video. To avoid error propagation, we jointly
generate wrist poses, local articulation, and camera motion in a shared world frame instead of
composing independent estimates. To support
metric-scale recovery, we condition on geometric features from the frozen VGGT- Ω \Omega backbone ( Wang et al., 2026 ) and supervise in metric space; hand-specific features add cues for local articulation. To handle ambiguous and missing observations, we learn a conditional
distribution over joint hand-camera motion using flow matching. Compared with regressing a single trajectory, this generative
formulation produces more accurate and temporally smoother motion, while exhibiting greater sample
diversity where the hand is unobserved.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
3D Hand Pose and Mesh Reconstruction: Large-scale models such as HaMeR ( Pavlakos et al., 2024 ) recover detailed articulated pose in the wild,
while WiLoR ( Potamias et al., 2025 ) additionally targets robust 3D hand localization. Interaction
and physical priors ( Zuo et al., 2023 ; Suzuki et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ) and spatio-temporal
context ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) further address occlusion and motion ambiguity. Recent work has explored
complementary strategies for monocular hand reconstruction, including contrastive pre-training in
SiMHand ( Lin et al., 2025 ) , controllable synthetic data generation in
SesaHand ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) , exemplar-based in-context reconstruction in
EgoHandICL ( Xie et al., 2026 ) , and kinematics-aware architectures in Rodrigues
Network ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) . Egocentric datasets and benchmarks capture hand-object
interactions ( Ohkawa et al., 2023 ; Fan et al., 2024 ) . HOPformer ( Bansal et al., 2026 ) models egocentric hand-object pose, and EgoForce ( Millerdurai et al., 2026 ) estimates camera-space hand pose.
These advances improve hand pose and shape, but a shared metric world trajectory also requires
camera motion.

blocks.en:
World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction: For full-body motion, WHAC ( Yin et al., 2024 ) jointly recovers metric human and camera trajectories.
For articulated hands, HaWoR ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) and
Dyn-HaMR ( Yu et al., 2025 ) construct global motion from camera-space hand estimates and separately
recovered camera trajectories. HandFlow ( Xu et al., 2026 ) learns camera-space hand motion distributions and
transforms its predictions into world coordinates using SLAM. StableHand ( Zeng et al., 2026 ) instead
learns world-space refinement of hand observations constructed from separate hand and camera estimates,
using quality-aware initialization to preserve reliable observations. UniHand ( Sun et al., 2026 ) generates hand motion through latent diffusion in a fixed coordinate system defined by the first
camera frame, but does not generate the camera trajectory. ReViV ( Lyu et al., 2026 ) jointly models camera
trajectories and camera-space hand kinematics, then aligns the reconstructed viewer and scene in a
metric frame. DewHand jointly generates metric hand and camera trajectories in a single stage, conditioned on geometric and hand-specific features.

blocks.en: 3.1 Problem Formulation and State Representation
blocks.zh: 3.1 问题的提出和国家代表

blocks.en:
Our goal is to recover the metric 3D motion of both hands and the camera in a common world frame.
We take the camera coordinate system of the first frame as the world frame, so that no external
localization, gravity estimate, or scene template is required at inference time.
The outputs in Fig. 3 are the camera pose ( 𝐑 t c , 𝐩 t c ) ∈ S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) × ℝ 3 (\mathbf{R}^{c}_{t},\mathbf{p}^{c}_{t})\in SO(3)\times\mathbb{R}^{3} and, for each hand h ∈ { L , R } h\in\{L,R\} , global wrist pose ( 𝐑 t h , 𝐩 t h ) ∈ S ​ O ​ ( 3 ) × ℝ 3 (\mathbf{R}^{h}_{t},\mathbf{p}^{h}_{t})\in SO(3)\times\mathbb{R}^{3} ,
local pose 𝜽 t h ∈ ℝ 15 × 6 \boldsymbol{\theta}^{h}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{15\times 6} , and clip-level shape 𝜷 h ∈ ℝ 10 \boldsymbol{\beta}^{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{10} ( Romero et al., 2017 ) . The local pose stores 6D rotations of
15 joints, converted to MANO’s 45D axis-angle pose for mesh decoding.
We group the quantities that live in the world frame into a global motion stream 𝐱 t global = ( 𝐑 t L , 𝐩 t L , 𝐑 t R , 𝐩 t R , 𝐑 t c , 𝐩 t c ) \mathbf{x}^{\mathrm{global}}_{t}=(\mathbf{R}^{L}_{t},\mathbf{p}^{L}_{t},\mathbf{R}^{R}_{t},\mathbf{p}^{R}_{t},\mathbf{R}^{c}_{t},\mathbf{p}^{c}_{t}) and the hand-local parameters into a local hand stream 𝐱 t local = ( 𝜽 t L , 𝜷 L , 𝜽 t R , 𝜷 R ) \mathbf{x}^{\mathrm{local}}_{t}=(\boldsymbol{\theta}^{L}_{t},\boldsymbol{\beta}^{L},\boldsymbol{\theta}^{R}_{t},\boldsymbol{\beta}^{R}) .
The clip-level shape target is repeated across frames in this stream.
This separation reflects the different geometry and conditioning cues of global rigid motion and
local articulation, while the two streams remain coupled throughout the model. Rotations are
parameterized by the 6D continuous representation ( Zhou et al., 2019 ) .

projection of its camera token to the pooled feature and project the sum into one geometry token 𝐜 t G \mathbf{c}^{G}_{t} per frame. HaMeR patch features are spatially pooled and projected into
separate left- and right-hand tokens 𝐜 t h \mathbf{c}^{h}_{t} , h ∈ { L , R } h\in\{L,R\} ; separate tokens keep a
missing or corrupted observation of one hand from affecting the other.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We addressed metric world-space reconstruction of two hands and the camera from monocular
egocentric video. DewHand jointly generates global hand and camera motion, local articulation,
and hand shape in a shared world frame, avoiding the composition of separately estimated
trajectories. Geometric and hand-specific features provide complementary cues for global placement
and articulation, while flow matching models motion under incomplete observations. On HOT3D and
ARCTIC, DewHand achieves the lowest rigid-aligned world-space hand error. The small gap between
rigid- and similarity-aligned hand errors further supports metric-scale recovery without scale
correction at evaluation. On HOT3D, it also improves metric camera scale recovery over the compared
SLAM systems. Camera supervision primarily
improves global hand placement, and flow matching yields more accurate and temporally consistent
motion than direct regression. Zero-shot results show the lowest rigid-aligned WA-MPJPE on HoloAssist,
H2O, and TACO, although other metrics do not always lead. Future work could
extend the model beyond fixed offline windows and incorporate manipulated objects and hand-object
contact.

和在共同的世界框架内的手形,避免单独估计的构成
轨迹. 几何特征和手性特征为全球定位提供了补充提示
